The detailed 15-1255.00 designs digital interfaces or websites and develops and tests layouts, navigation functions, compatibility, and usability. This page uses the same-SOC separate series for US wages and employment, without mixing in the developer aggregate.
Inputs include user tasks, product goals, content, device and browser scope, design specifications, and development constraints; lawful use of materials and real user data are verified separately.
Tasks cover user research, visual concepts, prototypes, style documentation, website testing, problem correction, and developer collaboration; the specific division of work varies by position.

Outputs include page or interaction prototypes, graphic and layout specifications, test and feedback records, and design specifications; a static screenshot cannot substitute for full functional validation.

Layout and visual design and interaction compatibility are the internal task focuses and may be combined in one position. The scope of research, design, and technical collaboration is verified against the actual division of work.

Communicate with product, users, front-end and back-end development, and related teams, explaining dimensions, states, and technical constraints; when feedback is unclear, clarify first, and do not substitute aesthetics for user evidence.

The detailed ONet interests IAC and Zone Four belong to the US preparation framework, and BLS states that education requirements vary by setting; a Chinese master's degree sample cannot be generalized to all positions.

Computer, design tool, and documentation work often requires prolonged sitting, attention to detail, and team communication, and working hours are verified per position; W29 uses no real client materials or user data.
Layout and visual design and interaction compatibility are the two internal task types, and both must turn product goals into checkable deliverables.

How do drawing layouts and checking interaction work together?

Layout focuses on information, visual hierarchy, and specifications, while interaction checks focus on states, paths, and device differences. The two combine, and a screenshot fitting the width does not mean real product usability or an accessibility pass.

Web and digital interface designers design the layout, navigation, function, and visual presentation of websites or digital interfaces, research user feedback, and test compatibility and usability across different browsers or devices; they may also work with client-side code, graphics, and content maintenance. An attractive visual is only part of the output — layout specifications, interaction states, test records, and developer collaboration also need verification.
Analyzes query intent and marketing metrics to optimize impressions; marketing performance differs from interface compatibility.
Analyzes business and application problems and systems integration; the systems requirement scope is broader.
Uses user support as an example of diagnosing hardware and software problems; the support target includes different subfields and is not merged into a single position.
Designs and implements data communications network and capacity options; network architecture differs from page layout.

Insufficient evidence: the original methods section of the GenUI study was additionally read (arXiv:2501.13145v1). The study ran in 2024 between month 9 and November, with 37 UX-related staff at the same North American technology company, including 11 UX designers; each completed a small one-week personal-time project with a designated tool, keeping a diary and taking part in interviews. Internal recruitment and referrals, mixed roles, and a qualitative task study cannot give a representative adoption rate, net time saving, rework quality, or job replacement causality for this occupation.

The editorial suggestion is to verify the material use, keep the original inputs and versions, calculate dimensions independently, and record untested states before giving feedback; this is not a full design test or compliance process.

The ONet user research, prototyping, design documentation, and compatibility testing tasks can locate the assistance steps and do not prove that AI independently researches real users or completes testing.
US education preparation, the Chinese sample position, and organizational data responsibility are verified separately, and drafts and certificates do not replace actual skill or authority.
Product goals, state specifications, material use, and real user testing are confirmed by the relevant people, and a paper width fit does not mean all devices pass accessibility.

NIST's fabrication, privacy, and source verification methods are general risk grounds used for this page's editorial suggestions, not a designer experiment or product compliance certification.

Paper only; the R0 container content width is 320 units, the two cards are 140 each, with only one 16 spacing between them and no padding, border, or other items. The problem's test only checks that the two cards plus spacing do not exceed the container width.
Wrong draft: "140×2=280, leaving 40, all devices are fully compatible and accessibility passes, so it can be released."
Task: error correction and the narrow-screen option
Person A keeps the R0 inputs unchanged, adds the spacing, corrects the remaining width, and withdraws all device compatibility, accessibility, and release guarantees.

Person B independently changes the container to 280 with the rest unchanged, and the card width cannot change. Wrapping is allowed and vertical spacing is not counted; give a solution fitting the problem premise, not treated as a real before-and-after redesign effect.
Reference answer: total width and wrapping

R0 and Person A: 140×2+16=296 and 320−296=24; only the problem's single row fits the width, and with no text, navigation, actual devices, or user testing given, it cannot be taken as fully compatible or accessible.

Person B: 280<296, so the original single row overflows by 16; one 140 card per row over two rows, with no same-row card spacing, leaving 280−140=140 per row. This is a solution fitting the problem premise, and the real states and experience are untested.
W29 | Full handover reference and deliverable boundaries

Recorder: trainee; intended reviewer: simulated design and development lead. The R0 fictional content width is 320, with two 140 cards and a single 16 spacing, and no border or padding. Person B independently uses a container of 280, where the original single row overflows by 16, so it becomes two rows of one 140 card each with no same-row spacing, leaving 140 per row; this only fits the problem premise and is not a real before-and-after redesign effect.

Unknowns: real text, interaction states, devices and browsers, user testing, accessibility evaluation, and material permission. These are to be verified by the real design, development, and testing responsible persons within scope; this simulated record was not sent and has no confirmation. title.text: Web and digital interface designers: tasks, wages, and layout experience | FermatMind

subject.name: Web and digital interface designers
subject.summary: Web and digital interface designers design the layout, navigation, function, and visual presentation of websites or digital interfaces, research user feedback, and test compatibility and usability across different browsers or devices; they may also work with client-side code, graphics, and content maintenance. An attractive visual is only part of the output — layout specifications, interaction states, test records, and developer collaboration also need verification.
